run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: Investigated the reported database connection timeouts for the blue-whale app in namespace app-94 with the database-troubleshooting runbook. Step 1 (application status): Deployment blue-whale was created 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z at revision 1 with 1 ready/available replica; pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-vt296 is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, created 09:11:50, and the only 6 events in the cluster (all Normal, 09:11:50–09:11:51) concern its creation. Step 2 (logs): fetch_pod_logs returned 0 lines for the current container and no previous instance exists, so no timeout text was readable. Step 3 (database service): Service postgres in app-94 (ClusterIP 10.96.136.45, 5432→5432, created 09:11:50) selects app=postgres-db, but its Endpoints object has subsets null, i.e. no ready addresses; the cluster-wide pod list (33 pods) contains only blue-whale in app-94 and no pod labeled app=postgres-db anywhere, the cluster-wide deployment list (25) contains no postgres/database workload, and app-94/postgres is the only postgres-like Service among 31 Services. Step 4 (in-pod connectivity test) could not be run, no exec tool is available. Step 5 (database health) is impossible, there is no database pod to query. Step 6 (pool config): the Deployment sets DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20; the app code comes from Secret blue-whale-app, which cannot be read, and the container defines no readiness or liveness probe, so Ready only means the process started. The app points at a Service with no backends, which is consistent with connection attempts to postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 timing out, but no metric, trace or log line of an actual timeout was observable: Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run and blue-whale is not among the trace services. Namespace app-94 itself was created at 09:11:50Z, only 39 seconds before the window end, so behaviour over the rest of the window is unknown. Whether a postgres workload was never deployed or the Service selector matches the wrong label could not be resolved, so the conclusion is partial and names the Service as the object where the fault is observable.

claims.text: The Deployment blue-whale in namespace app-94 was created at 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z at revision 1, has replicas=1, readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1, runs image python:3.9-slim with command ["python","/app/app.py"], and sets env DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20; it defines no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe for the blue-whale container.

The pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-vt296 (owned by ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5, which was created 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z by Deployment blue-whale) is phase Running, all conditions True including Ready and ContainersReady, with container blue-whale restartCount 0, no lastState, created 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z.

Namespace app-94 contains exactly two Services, both created 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z: blue-whale (ClusterIP 10.96.135.53, port 8080, selector app=blue-whale) and postgres (ClusterIP 10.96.136.45, port 5432 targeting 5432, selector app=postgres-db).

The Endpoints object postgres in namespace app-94 has subsets null, i.e. no ready backend addresses for the port the blue-whale app is configured to use (postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432); the blue-whale Endpoints object by contrast has address 10.244.0.30 pointing at pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-vt296.

Cluster-wide there are 33 pods and only one of them, blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-vt296, is in namespace app-94; none of the 33 pods carries the label app=postgres-db that the postgres Service in app-94 selects.

Cluster-wide there are 25 Deployments and none is a postgres or other database workload; blue-whale in app-94 is the only Deployment in that namespace, and app-94/postgres is the only Service in the cluster whose name matches postgres, sql or db (checked over 31 Services).

Namespace app-94 was created at 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z, i.e. 39 seconds before the authorized window end (2026-11-22T09:12:29Z), so the namespace and this workload existed for only the last part of the sampled window.

Events across all namespaces inside the window number 6 and are all Normal and all for app-94 objects at 2026-11-22T09:11:50–09:11:51Z: Pod Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet ("Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1"); no Warning event and no event involving a postgres object was returned.
The only ConfigMap in namespace app-94 is kube-root-ca.crt (created 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z); no application or fault-injection ConfigMap is present in that namespace.

The database connection timeouts reported for blue-whale are consistent with the Service app-94/postgres having no endpoints: the Service selects app=postgres-db, no pod in the cluster carries that label, so traffic sent to postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 from pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-vt296 has no backend to reach and connection attempts would fail or hang until DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT (30s) elapses. Actual timeout error text could not be observed because pod logs returned no lines and metrics/traces were unavailable.

An alternative to a Service-selector mismatch is that the postgres database workload was never deployed: no Deployment (25 checked) and no StatefulSet for postgres exists in the cluster and no pod carries a postgres image or an app=postgres-db label, so both the label mismatch and the absent workload remain possible and the evidence cannot distinguish which applies.

The app's own database settings (DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20) were considered as a contributing cause, but no log, metric or trace evidence of pool exhaustion or in-app connection errors was obtainable, so this remains unverified rather than supported.

The blue-whale pod presents as healthy in Kubernetes terms (Running, Ready, 0 restarts, no previous container instance), which argues against a crash-loop or OOM cause; but because the Deployment defines no readiness or liveness probe, Ready only proves the container process started and does not prove the database path works.

Blue-whale being killed or crash-looping (OOMKilled, BackOff, CrashLoopBackOff) was rejected: the container has restartCount 0 with no lastState, no previous container instance exists, and the only events in the window are Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/SuccessfulCreate/ScalingReplicaSet events.

Restore a reachable database behind postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432: either deploy the postgres workload with label app=postgres-db (matching the existing Service selector) or correct the Service selector to the label the database workload actually carries, then confirm the Endpoints object app-94/postgres gains addresses before re-testing blue-whale.

Add a readiness probe that exercises the database path (or a startup check) to the blue-whale container so that a pod with an unreachable database is not reported Ready, and capture application stdout so connection errors become observable.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every query in this Run (get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, latency, kube_endpoint_address_available or other metric reading exists for app-94/postgres or blue-whale.

Jaeger was unreachable for every query in this Run (traces_list_services and traces_search for frontend and blue-whale returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE / INVALID_PARAMS), and blue-whale is not among the trace services listed for the target, so no span evidence of a failing database call exists.

fetch_pod_logs for pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-vt296 returned 0 lines for the current container (view status no_data) and the previous instance is unavailable, so the exact timeout error text, retry pattern and timing reported in the alert could not be verified.

The application code is mounted from Secret blue-whale-app, which cannot be read, so how the app connects (driver, timeouts, retries) and whether it deliberately injects DB faults could not be verified.

Queries for NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota and pods labeled app=postgres-db in app-94 and cluster-wide returned empty results (view status no_data: 457695d1-4782-4e38-8b2c-9e15cdc8adbc-t1:11ba70ec-dc3f-4a4b-b564-313ac4591e89, 457695d1-4782-4e38-8b2c-9e15cdc8adbc-t2:f47e4dec-5fa8-44fd-9b22-b44ec6db4c50, 457695d1-4782-4e38-8b2c-9e15cdc8adbc-t0:72b3a8bc-e1d6-4092-86d5-3e5fb8e839bb, e32bc085-0624-4b7a-8b49-7cae5db3c76d-t0:12af2fb6-a499-42f0-8937-80eb2fadf6a6), which only shows those queries matched no objects; network-policy blocking of port 5432 and quota-driven absence were therefore not ruled out.

Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so what created or changed the app-94 objects at 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z, and whether a postgres workload existed and was removed earlier, is unknown.
Namespace app-94 and its objects were created at 2026-11-22T09:11:50Z, only ~39 seconds before the authorized window end, so nothing is known about blue-whale behaviour earlier in the 24-hour window.
Whether the reported timeouts are constant or intermittent, and which requests were affected, is unknown: no logs, metrics or traces were obtainable for the workload.

No exec/connectivity tool was available, so the runbook's step 4 (nc/psql from the app pod to the database host and port) could not be carried out, and step 5 (querying the database's own health) is impossible because no database pod exists.
next_steps: Check the intended manifest set for namespace app-94 to determine whether a postgres Deployment/StatefulSet was supposed to exist and whether its pod label is app=postgres-db; compare with the Service postgres selector.

After a database backend exists, verify Endpoints app-94/postgres has addresses and run an in-pod connectivity test (e.g. nc -zv postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local 5432) plus a minimal psql/SELECT 1 before re-testing blue-whale.
Review Secret blue-whale-app (application code) for the DB connection logic and logging level, and confirm whether connection errors are written to stdout.

Once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable again, query kube_endpoint_address_available{namespace="app-94",endpoint="postgres"} and any app-level error/latency series for blue-whale to size the failure window and confirm the timeout signature.
Compare with the sibling otel-demo deployment pattern in namespace otel-demo (health probes, Service selectors) as a reference for how the blue-whale database deployment and probes should be defined.
